title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 270 (Winding up of company)

content.overview: Section 270 provides that the provisions of Part I of Chapter XX shall apply to the winding up of a company by the Tribunal under this Act. The earlier dual mode under the Act (Tribunal winding up and voluntary winding up) has been restructured: voluntary winding up under the Companies Act has been omitted and is now governed by the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. The surviving mode of winding up under the Companies Act is winding up by the Tribunal on the grounds in section 271, on a petition under section 272.
content.glance: Chapter XX Part I applies to Tribunal winding up under the Act; voluntary winding up under the Companies Act omitted — use IBC; surviving Act mode is Tribunal winding up (ss. 271–272).
content.study: The provisions of Part I shall apply to the winding up of a company by the Tribunal under this Act. Current-law framing: identify that the Companies Act route for winding up is by the Tribunal; voluntary winding up under the Act is omitted and is under the IBC; grounds are in s. 271; petitioners are in s. 272. Do not plead omitted voluntary-winding-up sections of the Act as current procedure.

sections.heading: Tribunal Winding Up
sections.body: Part I of Chapter XX applies to winding up of a company by the Tribunal under this Act.

sections.heading: Voluntary Winding Up
sections.body: Voluntary winding up under the Companies Act has been omitted; members' or creditors' voluntary liquidation is under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.

sections.heading: Connected Provisions
sections.body: Grounds: s. 271; who may petition: s. 272; liquidator appointment: s. 275; Tribunal jurisdiction after order: s. 280.

examples.title: Tribunal route
examples.body: A company is sought to be wound up on the just and equitable ground. The petition is under ss. 271–272 before the Tribunal; s. 270 confirms that Part I of Chapter XX applies to that Tribunal winding up.

examples.title: Voluntary liquidation not under Act
examples.body: Members wish to wind up a solvent company voluntarily. That process is under the IBC voluntary liquidation framework, not under omitted Companies Act voluntary-winding-up provisions.

hypotheticals.question: Is voluntary winding up still available under the Companies Act after s. 270?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Voluntary winding up under the Companies Act has been omitted. Voluntary liquidation of a corporate person is under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. The surviving Act mode is winding up by the Tribunal.

misconceptions.trap: Companies can still use the old Companies Act voluntary winding-up procedure.
misconceptions.correction: Voluntary winding up under the Companies Act has been omitted. Use the IBC voluntary liquidation route. Tribunal winding up under ss. 271–272 remains.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 270 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm Tribunal winding up under Part I. II. Note voluntary route is under IBC. III. Link to ss. 271–272. IV. Conclude.
